hypothesis: Choosing prompt lookup only when its expected committed tokens per elapsed millisecond exceeds MTP3 may beat the already rejected unconditional hybrid.
scope: The frozen Python rename and JSON unit-conversion development fixtures from section 2.36. Standard Rust/JSON generation already failed lookup eligibility in section 2.35.

fixed_choices.models_and_settings: Original target, Q4_K draft head, dynamic vocabulary 16384, ub512, installed runtime configuration.
fixed_choices.forbidden_retuning: No length, fixture, layer, type or performance-threshold sweep.

steps: Replay the pinned stateless lookup algorithm on saved output tokens. Verify source/tokenizer/input hashes and reconcile native prompt token counts.

Capture a bounded diagnostic with compact per-round start, selected-source and acceptance records. Include rejected-draft rollback/replay in the originating round, and reconcile drafted/accepted counters with responses.
Compare measured full-length lookup-round cost with the MTP3 committed-token rate. Report costs and acceptance separately; do not price verification from an unrelated target-only batch benchmark.
Screen an optimistic selection oracle before building an online controller. Any replay uses development outputs and measured cost estimates, not unseen counterfactual runtime measurements.

Implement a bounded causal policy only if the oracle clears at least 3% on both frozen cases. Otherwise stop, retaining the evidence. A surviving implementation still needs uninstrumented opposite-order performance and output/quality checks.

capture.request_order: Python, JSON warmups; Python, JSON, JSON, Python measured requests
capture.instrumentation: Four compact log sites: round start, source selection, checkpoint rollback and final acceptance. Monotonic ggml_time_us timestamps; source selection is after draft generation; acceptance is before response-token rendering.
capture.pricing: Report both median cost by source/acceptance and an optimistic minimum observed full-length lookup cost. Keep terminal truncated proposals separate.
capture.oracle: Dynamic programming on the fixed generated token stream. MTP always commits four tokens at the measured baseline cost; lookup commits its exact replayed acceptance plus a bonus token, at the minimum measured full-length lookup cost, with free selection and no exploration overhead. This deliberately optimistic model is not a literal end-to-end bound.

limits: Diagnostic instrumentation is not promotion-quality throughput evidence.
100% MTP acceptance in recorded runs does not prove acceptance at unobserved future boundaries.
Skipping bad lookup rounds cannot be counted as improvement over pure MTP unless useful lookup rounds actually beat that baseline.
No upstream engine or model feature is attributed as a new local gain.
